title: What Is RFM? Definition, Purpose, and Examples | Mailchimp

facts.fact: The page states that most companies score RFM factors on a scale between 1 and 5, though any values can be used.
facts.quote: Most companies use a scale between 1 and 5, but you can use any values you think are necessary and helpful in evaluating clients.

facts.fact: The page says customers who made a recent purchase, typically within the last few weeks, are most likely to make a repeat purchase.
facts.quote: Customers who have made a recent purchase, typically within the last few weeks, still have the product and brand on their minds and are most likely to make a repeat purchase.

facts.fact: The page gives a car company as an example of a business whose customers may buy only once, with a single car sold to an individual within ten years.
facts.quote: For example, a car company might sell a single car to an individual within ten years.

facts.fact: In the page's recency example, a customer who purchased the most recently receives a recency score of 5 on the 1-to-5 scale.
facts.quote: Individuals who purchased a product or service most recently would receive a score of 5.

facts.fact: In the page's recency example, a customer who bought a product last week would likely receive a recency score of 4 or 3, depending on other customers' purchase timing.
facts.quote: In this case, customer A would receive a 5, while customer B would likely receive a 4 or 3, depending on how recently other customers have made a purchase.

facts.fact: In the page's frequency example, customer A makes 2 purchases in a month and customer B makes 8 purchases in the same period, so customer B scores higher on frequency.
facts.quote: if customer A makes 2 purchases in a month and customer B makes 8 purchases in the same period, customer B would score higher in the frequency column.
